findings.problem: status is a public String field, allowing any arbitrary value (e.g. "sent" with is_sent=false, "unknown", "SENT"). The domain invariant that status reflects an atomic lifecycle position cannot be enforced by the type system.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct or mutate a LeaseWorkflow into an inconsistent state such as status="pending" with is_sent=true, or status="SENT" (wrong case), violating the intended state machine.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a sealed enum typestate (e.g. `pub enum LeaseStatus { Pending, Sent }`) and make it the sole lifecycle carrier. Remove is_sent and is_validated bool flags.

findings.problem: is_validated (bool) and is_sent (bool) are independent flags that encode lifecycle state. The compiler cannot prevent states like (is_validated=false, is_sent=true) or (is_validated=true, is_sent=true) depending on intended invariants. This is the classic bool-lifecycle-anti-pattern.
findings.failure_mode: Logical contradictions in lifecycle: a lease can be marked sent without validation, or validated without being sent, or both. No single source of truth for the workflow state.
findings.fix: Collapse is_validated and is_sent into a single typed enum or typestate machine (e.g. `enum LeaseState { Unvalidated, Validated, Sent }`). The enum variant encodes the complete lifecycle position. Remove both bool fields.

findings.problem: id is a raw `String` with no domain constraints or newtype wrapper. Lease identifiers in a domain model should be a `LeaseId` newtype that validates format/length at construction.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, malformed IDs, or IDs exceeding domain limits can flow through the core unvalidated, causing silent corruption or downstream failures.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct LeaseId(String)` (or a fixed-size `[u8; N]` if applicable) with a `new()` constructor that validates and returns a domain error on invalid input. Use `LeaseId` in the struct.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs mutation on a struct with raw string fields and no validation. It should accept validated domain types and return a Result or new typestate, not mutate a flat struct in place.
findings.failure_mode: The transition function has no guard against invalid preconditions (e.g. can mark any lease as sent regardless of validation state). No error path for forbidden transitions.
findings.fix: Sign the function as `pub fn mark_sent(lease: LeaseWorkflow) -> Result<LeaseWorkflow, LeaseTransitionError>` and encode allowed transitions in the typestate enum. Return a domain error if the transition is invalid.

findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow has no constructor. All fields are public and unvalidated. There is no boundary between raw input and trusted data — any caller can build the struct with arbitrary values.
findings.failure_mode: Every consumer can bypass all domain invariants by directly constructing the struct with `LeaseWorkflow { .. }`.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a `LeaseWorkflow::new(id: LeaseId, initial_state: LeaseStatus) -> Result<Self, LeaseError>` constructor. Remove pub visibility from all fields.

findings.problem: mark_sent sets status via raw string literal `"sent".to_string()` instead of an enum variant or typed transition. This is a fragile, error-prone pattern that bypasses compile-time guarantees.
findings.failure_mode: A future maintainer can typo the string, use the wrong case, or set it to an unexpected value, silently corrupting state.
findings.fix: Replace `item.status = "sent".to_string()` with an enum assignment like `item.status = LeaseStatus::Sent` (after converting String to the enum, or better, after replacing the String field with the enum).

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler or allocation analysis exists
no second-ring review or black-hat review evidence
no command evidence (no cargo test, cargo fmt, or clippy output)
no state-machine transition table or invariants document
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. The crate is a minimal stub with pervasive type-system violations: raw String for status, bool flags for lifecycle, no constructors, no domain errors, no validation. These are structural BLOCKERs that prevent any meaningful Holzman Rust compliance regardless of later additions.
